results.proposal_summary: The Nature for Health (N4H) Phase II Expression of Interest, funded by Germany's BMUV through IKI with an initial €50 million contribution, invites government entities from OECD DAC ODA-eligible countries (national, sub-national, or regional intergovernmental entities) to apply for seed funding of up to USD 2,250,000 per proposal to implement preventative One Health approaches that integrate biodiversity and nature-health concerns to reduce pandemic risk. Up to six proposals will be selected. The application window ran from 10 January 2025 to 7 April 2025 (now closed), with partners selected by August 2025. Non-governmental entities are explicitly ineligible. No co-financing is generally required. Implementation spans 2–3 years, covering a scoping phase (~$250,000) followed by full implementation (~$2,000,000).
results.ilo_match_evidence: The call focuses on biodiversity, pandemic prevention, and One Health nature-health integration, which falls almost entirely outside the ILO's mandate of labour standards, employment, social protection, and decent work.

results.proposal_summary: The Malaysia-UN SDG Trust Fund 2024/2025 Call for Proposals is a partnership between the United Nations in Malaysia and Yayasan Matlamat Pembangunan Mampan Malaysia (Yayasan MySDG), supported by Malaysia's Ministry of Finance, with an approximate total budget of USD 4 million. The Fund supports people-centric SDG projects in Malaysia targeting marginalized and disadvantaged groups across three thematic pillars: People and Prosperity, Planet, and Peace and Partnership. Eligible applicants include Malaysia-based CSOs, NGOs, non-profit organizations, academic institutions, and think-tanks (NUNOs), as well as UN agencies that are members of the Malaysia UN Country Team and have signed the Fund's MOU (PUNOs). Individual grants range from USD 100,000 to USD 500,000 per proposal, with project durations of 6 to 18 months. The submission deadline was 4 November 2024, and this call is now closed.
results.ilo_match_evidence: The call's priority areas directly overlap with ILO's mandate, including social protection for informal workers, decent work promotion, skills training, labour migration and refugee inclusion, and socioeconomic rights for marginalized groups, making it highly relevant to ILO's programmatic work in Malaysia.

results.proposal_summary: This is a Finnish domestic grant scheme based on the Law on Agricultural Structural Support (Laki maatalouden rakennetuista 1476/2007), administered by the Economic Development Centre of Uusimaa under the Finnish State Treasury. The call is open from 1 January 2026 to 31 December 2027 and targets agricultural structural investments in Finland. No funding amounts are specified, and applications are only accepted in Finnish or Swedish. The ILO is not eligible as this is a domestic agricultural subsidy scheme restricted to Finland-based entities with no provision for UN agencies or international organisations.

results.proposal_summary: CAF – Development Bank of Latin America and the Caribbean – launches the eighth edition of the Financial Inclusion Lab (LIF 2026), open from August 25 to October 18, 2026, seeking technology-based startups developing digital solutions for financial inclusion and education targeting the 'silver economy' (persons aged 50+) and MSMEs led by older adults in Latin America and the Caribbean. Eligible applicants are legally constituted private entities with active market operations generating revenue in CAF member countries, operating in growth/scaling stages. No cash grant is awarded; instead, the 20 most promising applicants are selected for a virtual Pitch Day, from which 8 winners receive a personalized acceleration program (January–May 2027) and an investment readiness/matchmaking program (May–September 2027) with ecosystem investors. The call is not open to intergovernmental organizations such as the ILO, and the primary objective is private-sector commercial scale-up and investment mobilisation.
results.ilo_match_evidence: While financial inclusion touches on decent work and social protection themes tangentially, the call is exclusively targeted at private fintech startups for commercial scale-up and investor matchmaking, with no alignment with ILO's mandate for technical assistance, labour standards, or social protection policy work.

results.proposal_summary: The Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS), through its Dakar regional office, is launching a comparative selection procedure for the grant-based assignment of initiative AID 013406 'GUIMARÉ – Sostegno integrato alla risicoltura di mangrovia per la sicurezza alimentare, l'empowerment femminile e la resilienza climatica in Repubblica di Guinea' to be implemented in Guinea. The total funding is €3,000,000 (non-reimbursable). Eligible applicants are exclusively Civil Society Organisations (OSC) and other non-profit entities registered in the Italian OSC registry under Article 26(3) of Law 125/2014, which may participate individually or as a Temporary Association of Purpose (ATS). results.proposal_summary: AICS (Italian Agency for Development Cooperation) launched this public comparative call on 30 September 2026 with a total budget of EUR 15,000,000 to finance synergistic initiatives proposed by Italian civil society organisations (OSCs) under the Technical Support Spending framework of the Global Fund for AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria. The call supports programmes aligned with the Global Fund Strategy 2023–2028 aimed at ending the three epidemics and achieving Universal Health Coverage by 2030. Eligible applicants are exclusively OSCs and non-profit entities registered in the Italian national list under Law 125/2014, Article 26, or consortia (ATS) led by such organisations. Applications must be submitted via the SISTAKE platform by 12 January 2027. Co-financing is a structural element of the instrument, and applicants must have prior platform accreditation.

results.proposal_summary: This AFD (Agence Française de Développement) landing page describes multiple grant co-financing mechanisms for civil society organizations (CSOs) and NGOs implementing international solidarity and development projects. The primary mechanism, the CSO Initiatives Platform, co-finances projects of at least €300,000–€500,000 (up to 80–90% of total budget) in DAC-eligible countries, targeting French and local CSOs for capacity building, education for development, and solidarity initiatives. Additional mechanisms include the now-suspended FISONG facility (innovative thematic projects), APCC (crisis/post-crisis calls), and FSOF (feminist organizations support fund). All eligible applicant types are CSOs, NGOs, French associations, foundations, and non-profit organizations; UN agencies and intergovernmental organizations are not eligible. No currently open call with a future deadline is presented on this aggregator page, and the FISONG has been suspended since 2023.
results.ilo_match_evidence: While some FISONG themes (social protection, financial inclusion of migrants, vocational training) touch on ILO mandate areas, the entire financing framework is exclusively designed for CSOs/NGOs and does not include UN agencies or IGOs as eligible applicants, making it structurally incompatible with ILO participation.
